scopeOutcomes.assessment: Bounded public search of Splunk Help release notes, Splunk Platform announcements and Cisco Newsroom. Read the 10.6 release introduction and upgrade links, the September 30 versioning section, and September 15 self-managed AI section. No version-specific 11.x timing, deployment, supported pairs, security baseline or Cloud availability was located in this pass. This is not proof of absence.

Current English Help matrix SOK to Splunk Enterprise version compatibility: 3.2.0, September 24, Kubernetes 1.32–1.37, Enterprise 10.0.12–10.6.0. Upgrade path guidance says Operator first. Changelog heading 3.2.0 (September 8) states Kubernetes 1.32–1.36 and Enterprise 10.6.0. Both record the Queue secretKeyRef change for Index & Ingestion Separation. Separately, the older localized matrix (October 1 indexed revision) still displays 9.4.15 as lower Enterprise endpoint. No source establishes 11.x compatibility.

Current validated architecture Deployment Options recommends clustered designs for redundancy and distinguishes single-site failure from multi-site recovery. Storage Considerations describes SmartStore remote storage plus local persistent hot data/configuration. Resilience and Scaling documents health probes, stateful storage and PDBs. Scope remains current Operator architecture, not 11.x requirements.

Application Lifecycle Management > App Framework describes declarative app distribution from object storage. Premium Apps separately identifies selected current ES and ITSI topologies and manual ES indexer add-on deployment. These operational patterns do not establish 11.x compatibility.

The exact 10.6 Workload management modes table reserves pools, categories and placement/monitoring rules for Advanced mode with writable CPU and memory cgroups. Basic mode supports admission rules only. Activate workload management on Kubernetes says allow_basic is false by default; mode status displays basic or advanced. These are current 10.6 documented behaviors.

Lantern Readiness sections Cloud migration team staffing plan, Developing and executing communications plan, and Post-migration staffing transition plan call for workforce planning, audience-specific communications and reassigned responsibilities. Planning guidance is not a migration procedure, entitlement, authorization or staffing guarantee.

September 30 Splunk announcement, Keep Apps and Integrations Ready for Updated Versioning, directs app and automation owners to supported product identification rather than version string alone. The directive concerns 10.6, not an announced 11.x release.

Cisco Newsroom Self-managed Splunk AI, accelerated by NVIDIA identifies available Kubernetes-based Cisco AI POD and self-managed AI Assistant, with Launchpad planned later in 2026 at announcement. No Enterprise 11.x architecture or later Launchpad delivery follows from it.
Fresh assessment of the complete registered claim families and scoped reader answer is outstanding.

The 10.4 upgrade guide heading TLS 1.0 and 1.1 support removed says removal is introduced in 10.4 for Enterprise across OSes. Retain both, plan TLS 1.2 or higher, and leave historical and unassessed tuples explicitly scoped. The candidate route and its reports retain the disagreement.

issueObservations.rationale: The current English 3.2.0 compatibility row and changelog give different Kubernetes ranges, Enterprise scope and dates. The older localized matrix still shows a different lower Enterprise patch. Exact combinations and 11.x must not be inferred.
The Enterprise 10.4 release table still describes TLS 1.0 and 1.1 as migration-only and off by default; the upgrade topic says they were removed in 10.4. The route retains both statements.

The 10.7 release history and managed service details supply distinct service milestones and product listings. 10.8 rollout and service details were also read; neither document establishes an individually applicable tenant pairing.
The Help matrix distinguishes its 10.6.1.0 and 10.6.1.1 rows. The latter names ES 8.8.x and retains the cohosted KV Store warning. Do not infer 10.6.1 or extrapolate managed service pairings.

Splunkbase appDetails.releases for ITSI 5.0.3 names platform lines 10.2 through 10.8. Help lists 5.0 for the 10.2 line and uses different scope elsewhere. The candidate corrects its stale package list; the exact Enterprise 10.2 maintenance patch remains unresolved.
The ITSI 5.0 known-issues topic retains ITSI-46607 under the observed 5.0.3 scope. Service discovery remains Preview and use depends on the exact documented conditions.
The ITSI 5.0 known-issues topic retains ITSI-46608 under the observed 5.0.3 scope. Keep it distinct from ITSI-46607 and from general release availability.
The Assistant features table still describes resumable threads and PDF download. Context limitations still describes access to the most recent interaction within 30 days. Reader and report keep both.

The detector-triggered use section still limits support to standard default metrics. The separate optimization section describes when custom metrics may contribute useful evidence. Reader and report preserve the distinction.

Both historical official path variants returned 404; the renamed official overview loaded and separately labels Triage and Autonomous Response. Remaining tenant and workflow conditions must still be assessed at the setup and linked task sections.

The 8.8 Export Enterprise and Cloud prerequisites give separate tested matrices. Export version progression does not establish App for SOAR pairing, Broker compatibility or an unlisted supported combination.

The indexed exact on-premises 8.8 title and 8.7 body label remain inconsistent. Bounded direct attempts did not yield the 8.8 known/fixed issue tables; do not assert individual fixes or label resolution.
The indexed App for SOAR 8.8 tested on-premises matrix includes the literal 8..0 cell. No normalized patch or supported pairing was inferred. Direct access remains separately recorded.

The 2.4 whats-new and current installer establish a conditional new installation path, while the 2.4 known-issues page repeats earlier planned and excluded wording. Keep Agent Mode, feature region, Model Runtime and user permission distinct from installation.

The current model Runtime section separately scopes external Azure model options, data processing mode and regulated conditions. Do not inherit Cloud Connected general processing claims for optional model selections.
